title: References
text:
2. Repos & tools

Runtime / harness [R]

Annulus (own) — local-first agentic platform; MVP is SWE, roadmap is MCP + GraphRAG + science/engineering platform.
karpathy/autoresearch — minimal autonomous research loop. Study-and-fork target; closest public analogue to Annulus’s second act.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — reference architecture: skills-as-procedural-memory, MCP, subagent delegation, programmatic tool calling, trajectory export.
NousResearch/hermes-agent-self-evolution — DSPy + GEPA evolutionary optimization of skills/prompts/code. Directly relevant to [M].
0xNyk/awesome-hermes-agent — community directory; useful map of the plugin/skill ecosystem.
Claude Code — terminal, repo-scale analysis and architecture. Skills are cross-agent portable (agentskills.io standard).
Cursor (Composer 2.5) — inline diffs + ADR review. Current daily driver.



Environments / verification [E]

PrimeIntellect-ai/verifiers — v1 (July 10, 2026) decomposes into tasksets / harnesses / runtimes. Dialect adapters for OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages.
Environments Hub — 2,500+ environments, doubles as a Python package registry (wheels + pyproject.toml).
PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-cli — install/upload/manage environments.
PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-environments — where RFCs and bounties land.
Harbor (fully supported third-party format in verifiers v1); NeMo Gym and OpenEnv in alpha.



Training / optimization [T]

PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-rl — FSDP, SFT + RL + evals, Slurm/K8s multi-node, VLM support.
Hugging Face TRL — local GRPO baseline; the “no managed infra” leg of the three-stack comparison.
Tinker + tinker-cookbook — GA since Dec 12, 2025. Primitives: forward_backward, optim_step, save_state, sample. LoRA-based. Checkpoint download supported.
NousResearch/atropos — RL environments framework for LLM trajectories.
tinker-atropos (Nous) — standalone Atropos ↔︎ Tinker integration; RL on real agent trajectories. The literal seam between the runtime and training pillars.



Meta / RSI [M]

OpenEvolve and similar open AlphaEvolve reproductions — evolutionary program search over a verifier.
DSPy / GEPA — prompt and program optimization.

title: References
text:
6. Open questions
Living list. Each one is a candidate notebook post or thesis discussion section.

Does an LLM fine-tuned with RLVR on Tesseract approach the self-play agent’s play strength, or plateau? Where exactly?
Can the AlphaZero-lineage agent serve as opponent and evaluator in an LLM RL loop for the same game?
What does the forgetting literature say about weight-updating self-improvement loops? Is forgetting the actual binding constraint on RSI, and does that argue for skills/memory-based improvement over weight updates?
What do Tinker’s primitives buy over TRL’s trainers that is not just convenience — and where does the abstraction leak?
Which of Hermes’s architectural choices (memory model, skills spec, security boundary) should Annulus adopt, and which are wrong for a local-first NASA context?
Where does evolutionary program search stop working — what problem structure does AlphaEvolve-style search require?

title: Ladder
text:
Each tool climbs four rungs. Only the last two count toward the portfolio.

Used — ran the quickstart, understood the surface.
Shipped — produced an artifact inside an anchor project.
Contributed — merged PR, published environment, or filed an issue with a reproduction.
Taught — wrote something that explains a non-obvious thing about it.

Code






One-time setup

Create an empty repo named lab on GitHub (no README, no .gitignore).
Unpack this archive, then:

cd lab
grep -rl johngrahamreynolds . | xargs sed -i '' 's/johngrahamreynolds/your-gh-handle/g'   # macOS
# on Linux: grep -rl johngrahamreynolds . | xargs sed -i 's/johngrahamreynolds/your-gh-handle/g'

git init && git add -A && git commit -m "scaffold lab notebook"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin git@github.com:your-gh-handle/lab.git
git push -u origin main

In the repo: Settings → Pages → Source = “Deploy from a branch” → gh-pages / root. The first push creates the branch via the Actions workflow.
Locally: quarto preview to write, quarto render then commit _freeze/ before pushing.

The template entry has draft: true, so it will not appear in the listing until you remove that line.

title: Scaffold
text:
Everything here is a stage in one loop: an agent acts, an environment verifies, a signal updates the agent, and the loop eventually closes on itself. Four pillars, one per stage. Every entry is tagged with the pillar it belongs to.


The agent loop itself: tool calling, memory, skills as procedural memory, subagent delegation, MCP, context management. Anchor project: Annulus — a local-first agentic platform whose MVP is software engineering and whose roadmap is a general platform for science and engineering. Reference implementations read against: Hermes Agent, Claude Code, autoresearch.



Task specification, reward design, eval harnesses, and the question of what counts as evidence that a system works. Anchor artifact: Tesseract as a verifiers environment, published to the Environments Hub. Governing rule for this pillar and the whole notebook: no claim without a rerunnable eval.



Turning verified signal into a better policy. Two legs that are deliberately distinct skill trees:

Classical deep RL — the thesis: an AlphaZero/MuZero-lineage self-play agent for Tesseract, from environment through truncated training to full-game self-play.
LLM post-training — GRPO/RLVR via TRL, prime-rl, Tinker, and Atropos.

The bridge between them is the shared Tesseract environment, which lets the same task be attacked by both pipelines and compared honestly.



Recursive self-improvement and agentic science: evolutionary program search, open-ended multi-agent discovery, autonomous research loops, formal-math agents. The specific question carried into this pillar from prior work: is catastrophic forgetting the binding constraint on weight-updating self-improvement, and if so does that argue for skill- and memory-based improvement instead?

How entries work

Every entry is tagged with one or more pillars.
Numbers come from a harness that reruns. Figures are generated by code in the entry, cached via Quarto’s freeze.
Negative results and dead ends get entries too. They are the point of a notebook.
Drafts live in the repo with draft: true and do not appear in the listing.
